To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decision of HIV-positive mothers to adopt preventive infant feeding practices is not only a personal decision but is the product of interactions between women, men and the health care system.

(i) the construction of decisions concerning infant feeding practices in the context of HIV is complex and involves several actors, (ii) men are involved in the construction of infant feeding decisions and practices and (iii) the project team plays a key role in the adoption and application of preventive options.
the decision to apply a preventive infant feeding option is not only the result of a woman's individual choices, but also of the interactions between the woman and her spouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of couples in the implementation of PMTCT programs, and the importance of the project team in the adoption of preventive options.
how the couple relationship and the social environment influence infant feeding decisions and practices.
the following question: what are the factors that influence the decision of a couple to choose a preventive option in the context of HIV transmission from mother to child?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PMTCT programs need to take into account the complexity of couple dynamics in order to maximize their impact on infant feeding decisions and practices.

(1) men are not always supportive of the decision of their HIV-positive partner to apply the advice received in PMTCT projects; (2) women are not always supported by their partner in their decision; (3) the project team is a key player in the adoption of preventative practices; (4) the decision of women to adopt a preventive infant feeding option is not always dependent on the decision of their spouse.
the PMTCT programs should take into consideration the role of the couple in the decision-making process and the implementation of the infant feeding options.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implementation of preventive options for couples is a complex process where the three groups of actors interact.
the decision making process for infant feeding practices is a social one, and not only a medical one.
PMTCT programs must take the role of men into consideration and that the role of the project team in the implementation of preventive options must be strengthened.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the involvement of men and the project staff in the prevention of mother-to-infant transmission of HIV should be strengthened.
the implementation of PMTCT programs requires a more comprehensive approach, taking into account the social and cultural context in which they are deployed.
the involvement of men is crucial to improving infant feeding practices.
